To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrical conductivity and oxygen transport in the SrFe1-xMo xO3-δ system depend strongly on the molybdate dopant concentration.
the molybdate substitution in SrFeO3-δ results in deterioration of p-type conductivity, while n-type conductivity is improved.

molybdenium doping of SrFeO3 − d results in the increase of oxygen-ion and n-type electron contributions to conductivity, which is explained in terms of the involvement of Mo cations in oxygen ion and electron transport.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of the dopant on the structural stability and electrical conductivity of perovskite SrFe1 – xMoxО3 – δ.
the effect of Mo doping on the electrical conductivity of SrFeO3 − d.
the influence of Mo substitution on the electrical transport in Sr(Fe1 − Mox)O3 −δ, where х = 0.05,0.1 and0.2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Mo-doping of SrFeO3 −δ leads to a considerable decrease of the oxygen-ion contribution to the conductivity.
the molybdate dopant is a good candidate for the development of n-type mixed ionic and electronic conducting materials for oxygen separation membranes.
the electrical conductivity of SrFe1 xMox O3 δ is controlled by the oxygen vacancies at low Mo content and by the Mo5+ cation at high Mo content.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the molybdate dopant is able to enhance the oxygen-ion transport at low dopant content, while the electron transport is favored at higher dopant content.
the electrical conductivity of SrFeO3 − doped with molybdate is mainly controlled by the oxygen-ion transport.
molybdenate substitution in SrFeO3 −δ is an effective method for enhancing the n-type conductivity and for improving the oxygen-ion transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the molybdate substitution can be used for the development of oxygen-conducting materials with enhanced oxygen transport properties.
the molybdate doping of SrFeO3 −δ is a promising approach to improve its electrical conductivity.

the Mo doping of the SrFeO3 −δ perovskite results in a significant change in the electrical transport mechanism, from p-type to n-type conductivity, which is of great interest for the development of mixed-conducting membranes for oxygen separation.
